explanation: Despite the historical RabinKarp name, this implementation uses KMP. Build a prefix table giving the longest proper border at every pattern position. On a mismatch, jump to a shorter known border instead of restarting the text scan. Python indexes Unicode code points directly; a non-BMP character before a match counts as one here but as two UTF-16 units in the other displayed implementations.
timeComplexity: O(n+m): prefix construction and text scanning advance their main index once; each fallback decreases matched, so total fallback steps are linear. KMP fallback decreases a prefix length previously increased by scans; rolling hashes cost constant time per window plus exact verification when hashes agree.
spaceComplexity: O(m) auxiliary prefix-table entries for a pattern of m Unicode code points, plus constant loop state; the text is not copied.
attribution: Original Python implementation authored for EPI Practice from its displayed contract and independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference source adapted.
correctness: The matched length is the longest pattern prefix equal to a suffix of text already scanned. A mismatch can only preserve a border of that prefix, and prefix-table jumps enumerate those possible shorter borders without skipping a match. Reaching the pattern length proves equality, and scanning text left to right yields the first match.
walkthrough: For text cedar-ridge and pattern ridge, prefix-table entries are all zero. The letters through cedar- leave no matched prefix. At index 6, r starts a match; i,d,g,e extend it to five characters by index 10. Return 10-5+1=6.
edgeCases: An empty pattern matches at index 0.
A pattern longer than the text cannot match.
Repeated matches return the first index; equal hashes alone never establish equality.
